utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: One hundred and fifty of you males were separated; right?

utterances.speaker: MILAZIM THAQI
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: I don't -- in the transcript it reads "157." I think I heard that from the translator. The summary indicated a different number. I just wanted to make sure the witness isn't being referred to something out of context.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What isn't correct? Could you explain this to me? I don't know what I quoted incorrectly. I'm not clear on that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether the accused quoted incorrectly, but in the summary we indicated he describes 147. The witness -- it was put to the witness 157.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: I don't know if it's translation or whatever. I just wanted, in fairness in the witness, to point that out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, we have that sorted out. Now, Mr. Thaqi, you know what you're being asked about, do you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, put your question again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Who told you that there were 157 of you? Did you count them or did somebody tell you that figure?

utterances.speaker: MILAZIM THAQI
utterances.text: I counted them myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you counted them yourself, did you?

utterances.speaker: MILAZIM THAQI
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Let me read on page 4 from the third paragraph of your statement. You say: "I have been told that there were 157 in total." That's what it states. "I have been told that there were ..." You don't count them. You say, "I have been told that there were ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: To be fair to the witness, the previous sentence -- just a moment. The previous sentence should be read. It says: "We were made to sit in four rows along the road. There were over 150 men altogether. I have been told that there were 157 in total. I was amongst the youngest ..."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't know what isn't fair to the witness, Mr. May. I asked him whether he counted them or whether he was told, and he said that he told them. In the statement it says that he was told. So I'm asking him which of the two is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember - I can look at it to check this out, but I don't think this is challenged - you said that in the field there were several thousand people there who had gathered together in the field, in the meadow. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILAZIM THAQI
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: How many thousand, roughly, would you say were there?

utterances.speaker: MILAZIM THAQI
utterances.text: Approximately 15.000, 16.000.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So 15.000, 16.000. Of those 15.000, 16.000 people, they singled out just 157; right? And you say they singled out the men, which means that the rest of the 15.000 were women and children and just 157 of you who were men; right?

utterances.speaker: MILAZIM THAQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. When they divided you up into two groups, you say that there were 33 persons in your group, which means that in the other group there were a remaining 144. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILAZIM THAQI
utterances.text: The first group, I counted them when they took us up in that place. We were 33 people. Three survived. Thirty were killed on the spot. But I can't tell you how many were in the other groups. That I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. You survived this execution. That is the substance of your statement. And you say that this group was taken off by one policeman, that you were taken off by one policeman; right?

utterances.speaker: MILAZIM THAQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And apart from this one policeman, there was nobody else with you, just this one policeman; right?

utterances.speaker: MILAZIM THAQI
utterances.text: I didn't see any other policemen, only that one. The others were -- remained below in the meadow.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you went two by two; right?

utterances.speaker: MILAZIM THAQI
utterances.text: When they separated us, when they told us to kneel, then they made us sit in rows of four but two by twos. They said, "We will take you to another place and the others to Klina." And this is how we went there, by twos.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And does that mean two rows, one behind the other? Right?

utterances.speaker: MILAZIM THAQI
utterances.text: We were in rows of twos.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Two by two. And when you turned towards them, you were in a -- in two lines?

utterances.speaker: MILAZIM THAQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And you were in the other line. Not in the first line but in the second line; right?

utterances.speaker: MILAZIM THAQI
utterances.text: The first line, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you -- that means that you were the closest there, the closest to the policeman who executed you, as you say.

utterances.speaker: MILAZIM THAQI
utterances.text: I was on the left-hand side of that policeman.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And how far away from you was he?

utterances.speaker: MILAZIM THAQI
utterances.text: Maybe seven or eight metres away, not more than that. I didn't measure it, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did that just one policeman shoot at you?

utterances.speaker: MILAZIM THAQI
utterances.text: Yes. He was the one who shot, but God saved us. And I'm here to tell the truth and only the truth, nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. So that means that he shot at you and missed you from a distance of seven metres. He shot a burst of gunfire at you. Now, how did these people all fall on top of you when you were in the first line and closest to him?

utterances.speaker: MILAZIM THAQI
utterances.text: I was on the left-hand side, I said, and I was saved by those two victims who fell over me after he shot at us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, you said a moment ago that nobody was in front of you, that you were at the head, up front.

utterances.speaker: MILAZIM THAQI
utterances.text: No. I was on the left-hand side, I said, but not exactly on the first line. I was in the middle.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But there were only two lines.

utterances.speaker: MILAZIM THAQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And you all knelt down on the ground; right?

utterances.speaker: MILAZIM THAQI
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, what about the people that were to the left and right of you? How far away were they? The one next to you who was shot and the one to your right and left, how far away were they from you?

utterances.speaker: MILAZIM THAQI
utterances.text: They were half a metre away from me. Not further than that. This is how we were all lined up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you were kneeling down on the ground. One of them was half a metre to the left of you, the other half a metre to the right of you, and they fell on top of you; right?

utterances.speaker: MILAZIM THAQI
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And who were the two men in the line in front of you? What were their names?

utterances.speaker: MILAZIM THAQI
utterances.text: I am not the so sure about their names. Uka and Isuf fell on top of me. Uka was on my right side, Isuf on my left side.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And who was in front of you then?

utterances.speaker: MILAZIM THAQI
utterances.text: There were many. I don't know their names because I didn't know each and every one of them by name. They were -- they had come from many other places.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What did the policemen shoot out of: a pistol, a machine-gun, what? What did he fire from?

utterances.speaker: MILAZIM THAQI
utterances.text: They fired with machine-gun, with heavy machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: A heavy machine-gun, you say. Well, let's say that he shot from a light machine-gun. It doesn't matter. It makes no difference whether it was light or not. But do you know that a machine-gun, from a distance of eight metres, can pierce two bodies, at all events, if not more?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The witness can only say what happened to him. He can only give his description of events.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Your description of events. You were kneeling down. To the left of you at half a metre was one man, to the right of you half a metre away from you was the other man. They were shooting at you from a machine-gun at a distance of eight metres. They missed you, and the two people half a metre away from you on the left and right kneeling down fell across you. Their bodies fell over you. One of them fell to your left side, the other fell to your right side, and you were left underneath them. Is that your description of events?

utterances.speaker: MILAZIM THAQI
utterances.text: Yes, that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Very well. Thank you. Now, do you know the policeman that you describe in your statement on page 5, paragraph 2?

utterances.speaker: MILAZIM THAQI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did that policeman shoot -- do the shooting at your whole group?

utterances.speaker: MILAZIM THAQI
utterances.text: He did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And later on, you discovered that you had three bullet holes on the back side of your jacket and shirt but that none of those bullets actually hit you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILAZIM THAQI
utterances.text: That is right. And it was only on the day that we buried them that I noticed the bullet holes in my clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, tell me, how could they be -- these bullet holes be on the back if this man shot at you and was standing in front of you? You say that it might have been from the side. You said that he shot from in front of you and not from the side.

utterances.speaker: MILAZIM THAQI
utterances.text: It was the same person who took us there to that place that shot at us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That's why I'm asking you. If he was in front of you and you have these bullets holes on the back, you say that maybe somebody shot from the side. How could you have got these bullet holes in the back if the person that was shooting shot in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MILAZIM THAQI
utterances.text: He was on our right-hand side, not in front of us. He was eight metres away from us. And then he fired his machine-gun at us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That means that he was shooting at all of you from the side and not from in front of you. Now tell me this: How did you discover that the other men were later liquidated? How did you find that out?

utterances.speaker: MILAZIM THAQI
utterances.text: After three minutes I felt faint, and then when I saw two victims that had fallen on top of me and the blood running from their injuries, and then after about 30 minutes, Demush Asllani started to moan, and then I said, "Keep up your courage, Demush. We are lucky to be alive." I said, "Don't make any noise." He said, "Who are you?" I said, "I am Milazim Thaqi from Broje." "And who you are you?" I said. The other one, Shaqir Halil from Vojnika. Then we said, "Look what has happened, how many victims are here." The third guy didn't talk with us at all. He was a little bit further up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And on the 1st of April, Demush Asllani, was he buried in your presence when you helped with this air -- burial, with the burial?

utterances.speaker: MILAZIM THAQI
utterances.text: Yes, we helped with the burial. We buried all of them, not only Demush Asllani.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But you did bury him, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MILAZIM THAQI
utterances.text: Yes, I did. His family were there, his son was there, and I was there too.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And that's where you buried them; right?

utterances.speaker: MILAZIM THAQI
utterances.text: Yes. There is a meadow there. A neighbour of them gave them a plot of land for us to bury them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And do you know who Alush Liri [as interpreted] is?

utterances.speaker: MILAZIM THAQI
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you remember somebody who filmed and made photographs, took photographs of the victims in Izbica?

utterances.speaker: MILAZIM THAQI
utterances.text: Liri Loshi is the person. He's the one who filmed the victims.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. That's who I'm asking you about. Do you know him?

utterances.speaker: MILAZIM THAQI
utterances.text: Yes. But you mentioned another name. That's why I said no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, perhaps my pronunciation wasn't precise enough. So that's my mistake then. So you know Alush Liri [as interpreted] who took pictures of the victims in that event that you're talking about. And do you know that he made up a list of the victims as well, that he drew up a list of victims and photographed the victims too?

utterances.speaker: MILAZIM THAQI
utterances.text: He did that that day. My cousin Sef and myself were there, and he had a camera with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And do you know that on the list the name of Demush Asllani does not appear, though you claim that he was buried there together with the others? Do you know that his name is not on that list?

utterances.speaker: MILAZIM THAQI
utterances.text: The truth is that he is on that list of the victims.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Will you now explain one thing for me? There were 16.000 people. You were singled out, 157 of you. You said 147 was killed. Is it true that the KLA organised the funeral?

utterances.speaker: MILAZIM THAQI
utterances.text: In the funeral there were civilians and KLA members, because they were there to help bury the victims.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And the next witness, Draga, also refers to the KLA. On page 6, in fact, paragraph 3, you can check. You said: "The funeral of the victims was organised by the KLA. Altogether, there was a total of 147 victims of the Serb massacre. Some of the bodies were taken by their families and buried elsewhere. One hundred and thirty were buried in the field in Izbica." Did you state that?

utterances.speaker: MILAZIM THAQI
utterances.text: I said there were civilians as well as KLA who helped us, and I was one of them. And we buried the victims. Some took away the bodies of the victims to bury elsewhere. There was a total of 147 victims.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Several, you said, but 130. So 17 were taken away and 130 were buried there. And you say that the burial of the victims was organised by the KLA. That is what it says on page 6, paragraph 3, of your statement. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILAZIM THAQI
utterances.text: I am saying that there were more civilians and less KLA members to help us bury the victims. That's all I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. In -- towards the end of paragraph 3 on page 6, there's a short sentence which reads: "The burial of the victims was organised by the KLA."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. We've been over this, Mr. Milosevic. If you have any -- Mr. Thaqi, don't bother to deal with it. You've dealt with it. Mr. Milosevic, you've got two minutes or so left.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. May.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In that case, is it true that out of those 15 or 16.000 people and everything that happened there, the people that were buried were actually members of the KLA killed in fighting with the police and the army? Is that true?

utterances.speaker: MILAZIM THAQI
utterances.text: Those whom we buried, they were not KLA members. They were all civilians aged 38 to children of young -- of six months and six weeks old, women, and elderly people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic, have you any questions? No. That concludes your examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Ryneveld?

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: One, if I may.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Mr. Thaqi, you appear to have been challenged in cross-examination about how it is that the bullet holes in your clothing could be on the back if you were in front. Just for clarification, when the shooting started, were you kneeling down?

utterances.speaker: MILAZIM THAQI
utterances.text: I was lying on the ground. From the position of kneeling I fell down and then I knew nothing of what happened. And as I said, I saw the bullet holes three days afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you. Just let me clarify. When the first shots rang out, as it were, were you already lying down or were you still in a kneeling position?

utterances.speaker: MILAZIM THAQI
utterances.text: I was in a kneeling position.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Were you facing the police officer, away from him, to the side of him? How were you kneeling?

utterances.speaker: MILAZIM THAQI
utterances.text: No. I was -- we were with our backs to him. This is what we told him to do. We were looking to the mountain, to the stream.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: So at that point is it your evidence - and please correct me if I'm wrong. I'm just trying to visualise what you're saying - you were facing away from the police officer, kneeling down so that your back would have been exposed to him? Is that it?

utterances.speaker: MILAZIM THAQI
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Fine. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MILAZIM THAQI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Thaqi, that concludes your evidence. Thank you for coming to the International Tribunal to give it. You are free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And I'm happy to know that there is justice in the world for people to tell the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let me return the photograph.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We can't hear.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Question first. According to this list of witnesses that I have, the latest one that I received, the next would be Draga Mustafa. We've had Naumann out of order. So Draga Mustafa, (redacted), Vllasi Azem, Hoxha Hani, Haxhiavdi Ismet, Berisha, et cetera. Is that the order in which we're going to hear the witnesses from Monday on or are there any other changes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: There will certainly be one and that is in the case of (redacted). No decision has been made about him yet. As for the remainder, Mr. Ryneveld, will they follow the order that appears on the latest list?

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: There will be a new list printed in a few moments that will be distributed, but the bottom line is yes, Mr. Draga is next. Unless you want me to start him now, and I'm happy to. He's the next witness. That will be followed by Hoxha and Mr. Haxhiavdi and Berisha.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And where's Vllasi? You have Vllasi here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. He's not going to give evidence. He's -- we've not admitted him. We ruled on that the other day.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm asking because he's on the list, and he appeared after what you said, Mr. May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. He should have been removed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Yes. And the list that will be distributed momentarily --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Draga Mustafa and then Hoxha Hani.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Yes. And then the list in the order that we had. So if he's looking at a previous list, the order stays the same and the only ones that are -- that will be -- are the three that are immediately after Draga we'll be missing, because we've had Naumann. We have had no ruling with respect to the next witness. And Vllasi, we've had a ruling and he will not be called. Then the list continues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I think, for completeness, it should be said that prosecuting counsel was withdrawing Mr. Vllasi for the moment, although they might reapply or reconsider having him called at a later stage in the trial. But he's not giving evidence at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: I see that we have a few moments. Did you wish me to call the next witness or are we breaking? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It would be convenient to adjourn. Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have an objection. In my opinion, even according to your Rules, after you tell the witness that his testimony is over, that it would not be correct to switch on his microphone after that and allow him to make speeches. This has already happened several times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It is a mere comment from the witness. They have come a long way. They've come a long way. They have been through, many of them, very great ordeals. It's therefore not inappropriate, if they wish to say a few words, to allow them to do so. You need not worry, Mr. Milosevic. It will have no effect on the evidence in the trial. Yes.
